Playbook.name: AD — Domain Trust Added/Removed or Domain Policy Modified - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A domain-level trust or policy change occurred (4706/4707 trust created/removed, 4713 Kerberos policy, 4716 trust info modified, 4739 domain policy changed). In JCB only 4739 occurs today (65/90d). Triage question: sanctioned domain/forest administration, or trust manipulation to enable cross-domain attacks?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Trust and domain-policy changes affect authentication across the whole forest; malicious changes enable SID-history injection and cross-domain compromise.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live).

InitialAssessment.Rule: Domain policy changes (4739) are extremely rare and almost always deliberate admin actions; every instance should be tied to a change record.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the domain trust/policy change is a sanctioned administrative action or unauthorised manipulation of the trust fabric.

Step.name: Detail the trust/policy change
Step.Purpose: Capture exactly which change occurred and by whom for change-record comparison.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("4706","4707","4713","4716","4739") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, event.code, host.name, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName, winlog.event_data.DomainName, winlog.event_data.TargetUserName | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: 4707 (trust removed) can break authentication - operationally urgent even if benign. 4706 (trust created) to an unexpected domain is a cross-domain attack setup.

Step.name: Actor's concurrent privileged directory activity
Step.Purpose: Trust changes alongside group/DACL/replication activity indicate a domain-takeover campaign.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName == "$username" AND event.code IN ("4662","4728","4732","4756","5136","4724") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS ops = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Any co-occurring Tier-0/replication/krbtgt activity by the same actor escalates this to a coordinated attack.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows a trust created to/removed from an unexpected domain by an unrecognised actor, or INV-02 shows a concurrent privileged campaign.
INV-01 shows a recognised domain admin making the change under an approved forest-level change record.
Change by a plausible admin but no change record located.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-TRUST-CHANGE, INV-02-TRUST-ACTOR to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Sanctioned forest/domain administration (trust or policy) under change control.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the change record; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: Manipulation of the trust fabric or domain policy to enable cross-domain attack.

SOCAction.Item: Engage IR; review and revert the trust/policy change.
Audit for SID-history injection and cross-domain access.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A domain-management tool making a policy change unexpectedly.

Indicators.Item: A known automation account per a broken job.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Verify the change against forest change management.
If unauthorised: engage IR, plan reversion.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Audit trust relationships and SID history; review cross-domain access.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Restrict trust/policy edit rights; alert on every trust change; back up trust config.

QualityChecks.Check: Only 4739 occurs in JCB today - the other codes are covered pre-emptively.
Trust changes are near-zero frequency; treat any as high-signal.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Authorised forest change confirmed and recorded.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Trust fabric reverted/validated; SID history audited; actor eradicated.
